national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, 2016 surgical strikes, 2019 Balakot airstrike and Operation Sindoor in 2025 are bold examples of India’s zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism. The Prime Minister was addressing the nation in his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ programme on Akashvani today. He said, the surgical strikes carried out by the Indian Army on terrorist hideouts in Pakistan in 2016 demonstrated to the world a new approach to India’s counter-terrorism policy. Mr Modi said India will mark the tenth anniversary of the cross-border surgical strike tomorrow. Speaking about Census 2027, Mr Modi said the first phase of the ongoing exercise is nearing completion across all States and Union Territories. He said data from more than 32 crore families has already been recorded so far. He urged people to participate in the drive and use self-enumeration facility. Mr Modi also called for greater public participation in cleanliness drives ahead of the birth anniversary of Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi on 2nd October. He cited examples of cleanliness initiatives from across the country. Prime Minister Modi said millions of young people have pledged to stay away from drugs under the Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan. He called for collective efforts to build a drug-free youth, while announcing health check-ups and meditation camps as part of the 100-week campaign. Speaking about One District, One Product initiative, Prime Minister Modi said it is creating new opportunities for amla growers and entrepreneurs at Pratapgarh in Uttar Pradesh, with around 100 processing units now operational and women’s self-help groups playing an important role. He said the initiative aims to take local products to national and global markets and urged people to promote the ‘Vocal for Local’ message during the upcoming festive season.

national_raw_news.title: 49 mins ago | National 59 India retain Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy at Chess Olympiad in Uzebkistan
national_raw_news.content: India defended the prestigious Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, finishing as the best overall nation after picking up a silver in the Open section and a bronze in the Women’s event. The Indian men played out a draw with Hungary and settled for the silver medal on a tie-break, while the women drew with Georgia to bring home the bronze in the Chess Olympiad that concluded today. This marks the third straight edition where India have won the trophy, having claimed it on home turf in 2022, during their historic double-gold campaign in Budapest in 2024, including the latest in Samarkand. The Uzbekistan team regained the gold medal in the open section after winning the final round game against Ukraine by a 2,5-1.5 points. The Uzbeks ended with 20 points out of a possible 22, winning as many as 10 rounds and losing a lone match against Germany. The Indian men ended up with 18 points and were tied for the second spot with Germany that defeated Holland. However, thanks to a better tie-break score, the Indian team ended with silver, while Germany had to be content with the bronze. In the women’s section, China annexed the gold with another fine performance against Vietnam, winning by a 3-1 margin. The Chinese team also ended with 20 points in all, a couple of points more than second-placed Kazakhstan.
